run.name: 07-product-promo
run.finalText:
I built the "Pulse 2" title sequence as a 6-second piece on a near-black background with electric orange (#FF5A1F) accents. The beat is 120 BPM (0.5 s per beat, 2 s per bar).

- **Feature words (0–2 s):** "40h battery", "Spatial audio" and "Pure silence" each land on a beat. Each one punches in with a scale or slide, then cuts out on the next beat. Full-frame orange flashes mark the cuts.
- **Product name (2 s, bar downbeat):** "PULSE 2" slams in at 190% scaling down to 100%, with an orange flash and two shockwave rings expanding from behind the title.
- **Call to action (3.2 s onward):** an orange "Available now" pill springs in under the title. It presses once at 4.5 s, then holds to the end.

Layers are named in the Main comp: "Beat flash", "Shockwave ring 1/2", "Word 1/2/3", "Title - PULSE 2", "CTA pill" and "CTA text". I checked the frames with a contact sheet and the frames read as intended.

Two choices you may want to change:
- **Comp length:** I set it to 6 s instead of the 10 s it was, since the sequence resolves at about 5 s. The pill holds for the last couple of seconds so the offer can be read.
- **Word readability:** The feature words are on screen for one beat (about 0.5 s) each. That's what makes them read as flashes, but it's short for reading. The critic flagged this. If you want them easier to read, I can hold each word for two beats and drop the flashes to one per bar.

Next steps I can take: a two-beat hold on the feature words, a sound-effects pass, or a variation with the pill entering on the next bar.
